record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: For porous media containing two fluid phases, what physical and thermodynamic model should be used for homogenization when surface tension and fluid-fluid interfaces are part of the pore-scale problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a porous medium with a periodic microstructure of period ε>0, whose pore space is occupied by two immiscible fluid phases separated by sharp (or diffuse) fluid–fluid interfaces on which surface tension acts. At the pore scale, the fluids are governed by an incompressible Navier–Stokes (or Stokes) system in each phase, supplemented by interfacial conditions enforcing jump of the normal stress proportional to mean curvature (Young–Laplace), continuity of velocity, and appropriate contact-angle/wetting conditions on the solid skeleton. Determine a physically and thermodynamically consistent pore-scale model (e.g., a sharp-interface Stokes/Navier–Stokes system with Young–Laplace conditions, or a diffuse-interface Navier–Stokes–Cahn–Hilliard or Navier–Stokes–Korteweg system) that:

(i) admits a well-posed two-scale homogenization limit as ε→0;
(ii) yields, in the limit, an effective Darcy-type macroscopic system for the saturation and phase velocities in which capillary pressure, relative permeabilities, and surface-tension contributions arise from explicit pore-scale cell problems; and
(iii) is consistent with the second law of thermodynamics (non-negative entropy production) at both the pore and effective scales.

Specify the pore-scale equations, interfacial/boundary conditions, and the resulting upscaled equations, and prove rigorous convergence of the homogenization procedure.
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works derive macroscopic two-phase flow laws by homogenizing pore-scale models that include surface tension—using either Navier–Stokes–Cahn–Hilliard/phase-field formulations or sharp-interface volume-averaging—obtaining modified Darcy laws with explicit surface-tension contributions. However, no single rigorously justified, thermodynamically consistent pore-scale model with a complete convergence proof has been universally accepted; rigorous results are restricted to simplified geometries or diffuse-interface approximations, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Upscaling and Effective Behavior for Two-Phase Porous-Medium Flow using a Diffuse Interface Model
status_evidence.snippet: Two-scale model incorporating pore-scale phase distribution and surface tension into Darcy-scale effective behavior using Navier–Stokes–Cahn–Hilliard.
status_evidence.claim: Diffuse-interface homogenization yielding macroscopic surface-tension contributions has been developed.

status_evidence.title: Homogenization of two-phase flow in porous media from Pore to Darcy Scale: A phase-field approach
status_evidence.snippet: Upscaled Cahn–Hilliard with Navier–Stokes and surface tension as volume force to derive macroscopic laws for saturation and velocities.
status_evidence.claim: Phase-field-based homogenization gives effective two-phase Darcy-type laws.

status_evidence.title: On upscaling pore-scale models for two-phase flow with evolving interfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Upscaling pore-scale models with evolving fluid-fluid interfaces under surface tension.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on rigorous upscaling with moving interfaces.
